10561: City of Soap Lake campground on the lake, owned and managed by the city, with a camp host.  It has 22 lakefront and 6 back-side RV sites and 15 primitive tent sites. --Claude
11114: Country inn and RV park in Dayville, in a craftsman house built in 1908 for the mill owner Walt Greenwell and converted into an inn in 1991, nine miles from the Sheep Rock Unit of the John Day Fossil Beds and the Thomas Condon Paleontology Center.  The seven full-hookup spaces behind the inn are each 60 ft long on level gravel, separated by grass and trees, and the five power-only sites are on the lawn and have picnic tables.  Guests share a community fire pit with a bar and grill, barbecue grills and horseshoe pits; the John Day River, the town park and playground, the Dayville Cafe, the Mercantile and the South Fork Mini Market & Gas are within walking distance, and there are swimming holes nearby.  EV charging costs $10 an hour or $30 a day, and an RV check-in before 2 p.m. costs $10; monthly winter rates, November through April, are by phone.  The inn also has rooms and an Airstream Bambi for glamping. --Claude
11120: High-desert resort on 16 acres at Frenchglen, surrounded by the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge and its marshes; it has 38 RV sites, 14 grass-and-shade tent sites and seven lodging options, from cabins to the two-bedroom Homestead.  EV charging is offered only at site 39, by advance reservation.  A two-night minimum applies over Memorial Day weekend, the 4th of July, the Steens Rim Run, the Frenchglen Jamboree and Labor Day weekend.  Frenchglen's small mercantile, gas station and restaurant are typically open from mid-March through October.  Cell service is limited, and the Wi-Fi is meant for email and browsing, not streaming; mosquitoes can be prevalent in late spring and early summer. --Claude
11126: RV park and 9-hole golf course near Grants Pass, beside the Applegate River.  It has 12 sites the resort calls waterfront and 12 standard sites, on wide paved lanes.  The clubhouse has a full bar, snacks and a patio, and there are a pro shop, a golf simulator and a snack bar; weddings are held under a wisteria-covered gazebo.  RV guests can add golf for $25 for two people all day, cart not included, and stays are limited to 29 days. --Claude
11128: RV resort on 400 ft of Rogue River frontage, minutes from downtown Grants Pass, on historic grounds with mature trees, a clubhouse and pool table, gardens, a pond and a dog park.  Its premium riverfront sites, big-rig pull-throughs and shaded back-ins all have concrete pads and cable TV, and there are three family restrooms.  Guests can reach the river directly for fishing and wading, and the public boat launch at John F. Fleming Memorial Park is a block away.  Aggressive breeds such as Pit Bulls and Rottweilers are not accepted. --Claude
11271: The Green Valley Grocery's RV park on US 93, the Great Basin Highway, at Ash Springs in Lincoln County, a stop on the way to the Extraterrestrial Highway; many sites have a picnic table and fire pit, and the whole park has striking mountain views. --Claude
11288: RV park in the center of Goldfield's historic district, within easy walking distance of local businesses, halfway between Reno and Las Vegas.  Goldfield, once the largest town in Nevada, boomed to 20,000 people after gold was found in 1902; it is now an art community and home to the International Car Forest and the Saint Barbara Grotto.  Bikes can be rented. --Claude
11471: Equestrian and events center in Buckeye that hosts rodeos, barrel races, roping and cutting events and weddings; it has horse stalls and The Tack Room restaurant on site, and besides its full-hookup RV park it has event sites with water and electric.  Reservations made more than 30 days ahead are subject to change. --Claude
11550: RV park in Rancho Perilla Estates, through the wrought-iron gates off AZ 80 in Douglas, next to the golf course.  Showers are paid hot showers, and there are washers and dryers.  Electric vehicles, and RVs with large solar battery packs, pay $0.18 per kWh or an extra flat $40 a night; each site takes two vehicles besides the RV, with overflow parking at $20 a month, and group sites are available.  Dogs over 50 lb are subject to approval.  The park also has Boxabl casitas, and the golf course is good for birding. --Claude
11557: Avery's RV Park, on the main highway through Springerville beside a gas station, a convenience store, a BBQ restaurant and a bar and music venue with a party garden, within reach of mountain ranges, hiking trails and fishing lakes. --Claude
11566: Dwell Outdoor Hospitality resort in Sierra Vista at the base of the Huachuca Mountains; its back-in sites are 55 to 65 ft long and 30 ft wide.  It has a dog park, a pet wash and private bathrooms with showers.  Open flames are allowed only at the sites with fire rings, and wood fires not at all; RVs must be RVIA approved.  The deposit is the whole reservation, and a cancellation costs $20. --Claude
12424: SMUD's 400-acre park around a 160-acre lake fed by the Folsom South Canal, 25 miles from downtown Sacramento, with 21 RV and 32 tent sites and a designated swimming beach.  Weekend stays take two nights, Friday and Saturday together; stays are limited to 14 days, and campers with reservations cannot enter after 10 p.m.  Boat trailers have been banned since March 14, 2025 to keep out the invasive golden mussel, and hand-launched craft are inspected on entry; boats are rented on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day to Labor Day.  The lake holds bass (catch and release only), bluegill, redear sunfish and crappie, and rainbow trout are stocked from November through March.  The Howard Ranch Trail is an easy seven-mile round trip across a working cattle ranch, so dogs stay home.  The park also rents Jupes, and outside firewood is not allowed. --Claude
12445: RV park among tall pines in Paradise, with gravel and asphalt pads on paved roads, back-in and pull-through sites and an on-site manager; it also has 16 storage spaces.  RVs must be no more than 20 years old (management may make exceptions); generators and open fires are not allowed, dogs may weigh no more than 40 lb, and a second pet costs $25 per stay.  Stays over 10 nights are arranged by phone or online application, at $550 to $650 a month.  The office is closed on Sundays. --Claude
12635: Daiva RV Resorts park beside 2,500 ft of the Rocky Saugeen River, on more than 25 acres, over 19 of them left natural with walking trails.  The river drops 30 ft over a hydro-electric dam: upstream is deep enough for swimming, diving, boating and fishing, and downstream suits nature hikes and fly-fishing.  It has a heated pool, a playground and a comfort station, horseshoe pits, shuffleboard courts and badminton and volleyball nets, and planned activities such as Christmas in July, movie nights, children's crafts, horseshoe and euchre tournaments and dances.  It also has seasonal sites and a cabin. --Claude
12638: Resort on 50 acres of White Lake lakefront, about 60 km west of Ottawa between Calabogie and Arnprior.  Each RV site is individually metered and has a fire pit, and sites range from full sun to full shade.  No tents; the campground page asks for trailers with washrooms.  It has a marina with gas at the docks, boat slips, boat rentals and boat storage, a saltwater pool, a recreation and games hall, a coffee shop, a fish-cleaning station and firewood.  White Lake hosts several bass tournaments a year and holds largemouth and smallmouth bass, northern pike, walleye, rock bass, yellow perch, pumpkinseed, brown bullhead and bluegill.  Cottages and chalets are also rented. --Claude
12639: Small family-owned campground on 42 acres of mostly natural forest in the Village of Warwick, Lambton County, with over 2 km of trails and a new dog park.  The camping area sits beside a 2-acre spring-fed lake, where motorized boats are not allowed, fishing is catch-and-release and there is no lifeguard.  Besides its powered sites it has off-grid sites, and each site takes one family with at most 2 adults and 2 pets.  Bottled drinking water and firewood are sold.  The name comes from the creek through the property, not from bears. --Claude
12663: Daiva RV Resorts park in woodland beside the Grand River, amid hundreds of acres of farmland, where mature cedars and maples surround each site and the shallow river is good for floating.  A heated pool sits in the center of the park, beside a playground and a picnic area.  The Grand Valley Trail and the Upper Grand Trailway, an old CPR line, are nearby, and the Luther Marsh Conservation Area down the street is one of Ontario's best bird-watching spots.  It also has seasonal and 11-month extended-season sites (park-model cottages with year-round access) and cabins. --Claude
12664: Daiva RV Resorts park among Precambrian rock and windswept pines on the shores of Stoney Lake in the Kawarthas, with pinery and lakeside sites.  It has a private sandy beach, boat docks and a launch, and canoe and kayak rentals for exploring the lake's hundreds of islands; the lake holds bass, walleye and muskie.  Petroglyphs Provincial Park, across the street, is a sacred Indigenous site holding the largest known concentration of rock carvings in Canada, along with hiking trails and McGinnis Lake, one of the few meromictic lakes in North America.  It also has seasonal sites and boat slips. --Claude
12695: Summerhill Resorts campground between the Outlet River and Sandbanks Provincial Park, whose beaches and freshwater dunes are on Lake Ontario; East Lake holds walleye, bass, sunfish and pike.  It rents boats, paddleboards, kayaks and canoes and has a playground, volleyball, horseshoes and a propane exchange.  It also rents cottages and log cabins and sells seasonal sites. --Claude
12697: Campground on the Saugeen River, a fly-fishing mecca, near Walkerton.  It rents kayaks, canoes and river tubes, and a free shuttle drops tubers at Maple Hill Dam for a float of about 1.5 to 2 hours back to camp; there are a children's fishing pond and free pedal carts.  Through the season there are 50/50 draws, potlucks, barbecues, fishing derbies, bingo, paint nights, the annual river run and weekend fly-fishing schools.  Outside firewood is not allowed; the campground provides local bundled wood.  The Lake Huron beaches at Port Elgin and Kincardine are a 30-minute drive.  It also rents bunkies, a Mongolian yurt, biodomes with hot tubs and saunas and a 3-bedroom trailer. --Claude
12698: Campground between Highway 17, the Trans-Canada, and the Serpent River, which empties into the North Shore of Lake Huron, midway between Sudbury and Sault Ste. Marie.  It has an inground pool, a playground, a private boat launch, a fishing pier, kayak rentals, a movie and book exchange and a pavilion, and hosts a weekly farmers market and food vendors through the week; a restaurant is across the street.  Its rustic log cabins are three on the river and two in the main campground, and boat and trailer storage is offered.  The office is open 7 days a week from May to mid-October, and check-in runs until 9 p.m. --Claude
12700: Family campground in Greely, in the Ottawa area, whose sites have picnic tables and fire pits.  The pool has no lifeguard, and adult swim is from 3:30 to 4:30 p.m.; there are kids' play areas, horseshoes and an RC track, and Halloween is held over the Labour Day long weekend.  Long weekends take a 3-night minimum.  Outside firewood is not allowed, pets are limited to two per site, aggressive dogs such as Pit Bulls and Rottweilers are not permitted, and visitors pay $5 a day.  It also rents a bunky. --Claude
12712: Campground of 252 lots near Moonbeam, 3 km in on Highway 581 from Highway 11, on spring-fed lakes up to 40 ft deep with sandy beaches and three small water slides for children.  A paving-stone path circles the lake, the lakes are good for swimming, pedal boats and kayaks, and there are three playgrounds and shuffleboard; fishing is free, and outboard motors are not allowed.  The chipstand is open daily from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m.  It also rents train apartments, a lofted bunkie and a deluxe cabin, and French is spoken. --Claude
